description: Synthetic security laboratory with known vulnerabilities for HermesShield benchmarking

lab_environment.description: Synthetic lab with multiple vulnerable services and configurations

vulnerabilities.name: Hardcoded SSH Private Key
vulnerabilities.description: SSH private key hardcoded in configuration file

evidence.content_sample:
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEowIBAAKCAQEA...
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----

vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Remove private key from config file; use SSH key agent or secure key management

attack_path_relationships.description: Private key enables SSH access for lateral movement

vulnerabilities.name: Open SSH Port with Weak Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: SSH service running with password authentication enabled and root login permitted
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Disable root login, disable password authentication, enforce key-based auth

attack_path_relationships.description: Weak SSH config allows exploitation of exposed private key
SSH access enables lateral movement to internal services

vulnerabilities.name: Exposed Internal HTTP API
vulnerabilities.description: Internal administrative HTTP API exposed on port 8080 without authentication

evidence.banner:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Werkzeug/2.3.7 Python/3.11.9
Content-Type: application/json

{"status": "admin", "endpoints": ["/users", "/config", "/logs"]}

vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Bind admin API to localhost only; implement authentication and authorization

attack_path_relationships.description: SSH access provides network access to internal API
Admin API allows configuration changes and data exfiltration

vulnerabilities.name: Sensitive Data in World-Readable File
vulnerabilities.description: Database credentials stored in world-readable configuration file

evidence.content_sample:
database:
  host: localhost
  port: 5432
  username: admin
  password: "SuperSecretPass123!"
  database: production

vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Restrict file permissions (chmod 600); use environment variables or secret manager

attack_path_relationships.description: Admin API access allows reading config files
Database credentials enable direct database access

vulnerabilities.name: PostgreSQL with Default Credentials
vulnerabilities.description: PostgreSQL database running with default postgres/postgres credentials
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Change default credentials; enforce strong passwords; restrict network access

attack_path_relationships.description: Database credentials from config file enable access
Database access allows data exfiltration and privilege escalation

vulnerabilities.name: Sudo with NOPASSWD for www-data User
vulnerabilities.description: Web server user (www-data) has passwordless sudo access to all commands
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Remove NOPASSWD; restrict sudo to specific commands; use dedicated service accounts

attack_path_relationships.description: Database compromise leads to web shell, then sudo escalation
Root access enables complete system compromise

vulnerabilities.name: Cron Job with World-Writable Script
vulnerabilities.description: Root cron job executes a world-writable script allowing privilege escalation
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Restrict script permissions; use absolute paths; run cron jobs with least privilege

attack_path_relationships.description: Sudo access allows writing to world-writable script

vulnerabilities.name: SMB Share with Anonymous Access
vulnerabilities.description: SMB file share accessible without authentication exposing sensitive files
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Disable anonymous access; implement authentication; restrict share permissions

attack_path_relationships.description: SMB share exposes config files with credentials

vulnerabilities.name: Weak SSL/TLS Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: Web server supports deprecated TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak cipher suites
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Disable TLS 1.0/1.1; disable weak ciphers; use valid certificate

vulnerabilities.name: Docker Socket Exposed to Container
vulnerabilities.description: Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) mounted into container allowing container escape
vulnerabilities.expected_remediation: Do not mount docker socket; use Docker API with restricted permissions

attack_path_relationships.description: Root access via cron allows docker socket access

attack_paths.name: Full Chain: SSH Key -> SSH Access -> Admin API -> Database -> Sudo -> Root
attack_paths.description: Complete attack chain from initial access to root compromise

attack_paths.name: Network Path: SMB -> Config Files -> Database
attack_paths.description: Anonymous SMB access leads to credential exposure and database compromise

attack_paths.name: Container Escape Path: Root Cron -> Docker Socket
attack_paths.description: Privilege escalation via cron leads to container escape via Docker socket
